THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, APRIL 26, 1932
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C S D REGISTRY
D 357
Boycott Pickets File
Petition For Transfer
Of Court Jurisdiction
Charges Of Oppression And Misrepresentation
Levelled At Former Chairman Of Municipal
Council In Connection With Case
RECENT SEIZURE OF JAPANESE GOODS
DURING BOYCOTT CAMPAIGN
Charges of oppressing the Chinese judiciary by political force and unprecedented "misrepresentations" are made against Brig.-Gen. E. B. Macnaghten, former chairman of the S.M.C. in a motion filed by four Chinese pickets with the Second Branch of the Kiangsu High Court, for a transfer of jurisdiction in a case where they have been charged with robbery, in connection with the seizure of Japanese goods. The case was an appeal lodged with the high court by the S.M.C. against the dismissal of a prosecution against the pickets on a robbery charge. In their motion the pickets asked that the appeal should be transferred to another Court for hearing, charging the Settlement authorities with failing to carry out their duties.
In dismissing the motion, the high court ruled that it should have been made to the Supreme Court of Nanking, or the court directly higher than the high court here where the appeal has been set down for hearing.
The ruling of the court reads: "When a motion for transfer of jurisdiction is made by the party concerned, it should be made to the competent court, according to Article 22 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The 'Competent Court,' according to Article 21, section 1, of the code, should mean the court which is the direct superior to it. This case is now before this court as a court of second instance, and therefore, applicants should make the motion for transfer of jurisdiction to the Supreme Court. The motion made by them to this court is apparently contrary to procedure."
Motion Filed
The motion filed by the pickets reads:
"The applicants hereby move for transfer of jurisdiction in the case in which they were charged with robbery. They had scattered in different directions after the dissolution of the Society and this explains why the summons could not be served on them and why they failed to appear on the date of hearing.
"The applicants now find that the case has been set again for hearing. They intended at first to appear and answer the charge at the time specified. However, after the outbreak of hostilities at Shanghai the Japanese Navy and Army troops and 'ronins' have, by relying on their might and force, carried away and massacred thousands of innocent residents everywhere in the Settlement. Law is of no avail and rights of persons have been trampled under foot. Even the Settlement authorities have failed to carry out the duties entrusted to them by the residents and have yielded to force, without having any courage of lodging a protest or filing a suit. This being the case, the injustice done to the injured parties can never be redressed. Neither is there any way open to them for complaint. This is really a catastrophe never experienced and a shame in modern history. Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten, Chairman of the S.M.C., however, in the course of his address at the annual ratepayers' meeting unthoughtfully remarked that the recent fighting in and around Shanghai resulted from the District Court's conniving at the anti-Japanese movement. It can also be gathered from his expressions that he has attacked the judgment rendered in this case by the court of first instance. It is submitted that such a case of oppressing the judiciary by means of political force and misrepresentations is unprecedented. Although there is a cessation of hostilities at present the agreement for withdrawal of troops has not yet been signed.
Hostilities Feared
It is, therefore, feared that further hostilities might break out. The right of policing has not yet been fully recovered by the S.M.C. and the Japanese "ronins" are still at large in their atrocious acts. As ordinary persons cannot avoid being carried away and massacred by them, the applicants, who had participated in the anti-Japanese movement, will be most deeply resented by them. In case they make their appearance in court this time, who can safely predict that the Japanese "ronins" would not stop in and carry them away? At that time the Municipal police would also say that they have no means of protection. The applicants are therefore trembling at the thought of it.
"In these circumstances the applicants find it necessary to invoke Art. 21 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and hereby submit this motion for transfer of jurisdiction, setting forth the grounds therefor in accordance with Articles 21 and 22 of the Code of Criminal Procedure so that the case may be tried by the Kiangsu High Court and the applicants may be safe from danger. Applicants: Kuh Yoong-ding, S. Sing-ming, Yuen Hai-chong, Chao Tsong-yen."

四名中国纠察队员向江苏高等法院第二分院提交动议，要求将一起涉及查扣日货而被控抢劫的案件移交管辖权。他们在动议中指控上海公共租界工部局（S.M.C.）前总董麦克纳格顿准将（Brig.-Gen. E. B. Macnaghten）利用政治力量压迫中国司法机关，并作出前所未有的“歪曲事实”之举。该案系工部局针对下级法院驳回对纠察队员抢劫罪起诉的决定而向高等法院提起的上诉。纠察队员在动议中请求将该上诉案移交另一法院审理，指控租界当局未能履行职责。

高等法院在驳回该动议时裁定，该动议本应向南京最高法院，或直接向在此受理上诉的高一级法院提出。

法院裁定如下：“当事人提出移交管辖权动议时，应根据《刑事诉讼法》第22条向有管辖权的法院提出。根据该法典第21条第1款，‘有管辖权的法院’应指其直接上级法院。本案现作为二审案件由本院审理，因此，申请人应向最高法院提出移交管辖权动议。他们向本院提出的动议显然违反程序。”

已提交动议
纠察队员提交的动议内容如下：
“申请人特此请求移交对其被控抢劫一案的管辖权。在该会社解散后，他们已四散各方，这解释了为何传票无法送达，以及为何他们未能在开庭日期出庭。
“申请人现获悉该案已重新排期开庭。他们起初打算在指定时间出庭应诉。然而，自上海战事爆发以来，日本海陆军部队及‘浪人’倚仗武力，在租界各地掳走并屠杀成千上万无辜居民。法律已不起作用，人身权利被践踏。甚至租界当局也未能履行居民赋予他们的职责，屈服于武力，缺乏勇气提出抗议或提起诉讼。既然如此，受害方所遭受的不公永远无法得到伸张。他们也无处申诉。这确实是现代史上从未经历过的灾难和耻辱。然而，工部局总董麦克纳格顿准将在年度纳税人大会上的讲话中，轻率地声称上海及其周边地区的近期战事是由于特区法院纵容反日运动所致。从他的言论中也可以看出，他攻击了初审法院对此案作出的判决。兹认为，这种利用政治力量压迫司法机关并歪曲事实的情况是前所未有的。虽然目前战事已停止，但撤军协议尚未签署。
担心战事再起
因此，人们担心可能会爆发进一步的战事。工部局尚未完全恢复警务权，日本‘浪人’仍在肆意施行暴行。由于普通人无法避免被他们掳走和屠杀，参与过反日运动的申请人将遭到他们极深的憎恨。如果他们此次出庭，谁能安全地预测日本‘浪人’不会闯入并将他们掳走？届时，巡捕房也会称他们无力提供保护。申请人一想到此便不寒而栗。
“在这种情况下，申请人认为有必要援引《刑事诉讼法》第21条，并据此提交本移交管辖权动议，按照《刑事诉讼法》第21条和第22条陈述理由，以便该案由江苏高等法院审理，使申请人免受危险。申请人：顾荣庭 (Kuh Yoong-ding)、宋思明 (S. Sing-ming)、阮海崇 (Yuen Hai-chong)、赵宗炎 (Chao Tsong-yen)。”

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury. Monday, April 25, 1932
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL
C. S. C. R. LIG.

Old Mixed Court
History Reviewed

International Tribunal
Idea Termed Absurd
By China Times

Commenting upon Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten's recent strictures upon the Special District Court in the International Settlement, the China Times declares that the right to exercise jurisdiction over Chinese subjects and non-extraterritorial foreign nationals in the foreign settlements is an inalienable attribute of China's State Sovereignty and therefore the Chinese nation is determined not only to reject any proposal for the so-called "internationalization" of those Courts but also to recover complete and unfettered control, the Kuo Min News Agency states in a summary on the editorial.

The editorial begins with a review of the history of the administration of justice in the Settlement, pointing out that neither by treaty nor in actual fact had the Chinese authorities (prior to 1911) relinquished judicial jurisdiction in the Settlement.

Revolution Of 1912

It was only by taking advantage of the disturbed conditions brought about by the Revolution of 1912 that the Foreign Consular Authorities in the Settlement "usurped" the Chinese administration of justice and appointed Chinese magistrates of their own.

By the rendition of the Mixed Court in 1926, therefore, the Chinese Government did not obtain any concession from the foreign authorities but merely recovered what had been usurped and wrongfully retained against both international law and treaty provisions.

Mixed Court Rendition

The editorial also deplores that at the time when the Mixed Court rendition agreement came up for revision, the Chinese Government should have failed to recover complete and unfettered jurisdiction over the Courts but had agreed to such important limitations upon the rights of the Courts as those providing that the judicial police attached to the Courts must be selected from nominees of the Municipal Council, that the power of prosecution must remain in the hands of the Municipal advocates, the procurators of the Courts having few or no powers; and finally, that the prisons attached to the Courts were to remain under the control of the Municipal Authorities.

Chinese Territory

After referring to the remarks made by Gen. Macnaghten in the course of his speech at the recent annual meeting of foreign rate-payers, the editorial declares, "We must impress upon Gen. Macnaghten and other foreign nationals of his mentality the fact that the International Settlement of Shanghai remains an integral part to Chinese territory and that the right of judicial jurisdiction in the Settlement is inherent in our State Sovereignty."

"Moreover, it should be emphasized that the Courts in the International Settlement must have for their object the dispensation of fair and unbiased justice (to all the litigants irrespective of nationality) and the maintenance of general order and security. The foreign residents must not deceive themselves that such Courts are established merely for the interests or must seek the satisfaction of foreign nationals and that the Courts ought to protect such interests to the prejudice of others."

International Court Idea

Concluding, the editorial points out the absurdity of the idea of establishing international courts in place of the present Chinese Courts. The defects inherent in such a system will render it absolutely impracticable.

For example, the administration of justice presupposes the existence of a uniform and definite set of laws. What law is this to be? Since foreign nationals are dissatisfied with Chinese Law, the latter would be ruled out. If the Law of any particular country (other than China) is to be administered, it is inconceivable how the nationals of other countries would be satisfied.

Moreover, how can the application of a foreign law to the overwhelming Chinese population in the Settlement be considered fair and just? If the law to be applied is to remain the Chinese law, then it is obvious that no foreigners can be more competent than the Chinese themselves to administer Chinese law. "We are at a complete loss to see how Gen. Macnaghten can invent a law which will meet with the satisfaction and approval of all the different nationalities resident in the Settlement." Moreover, "under what authorities is jurisdiction over these Courts to be placed? The Chinese Government? The British Government? or the Municipal Council?" the editorial asks. Certain other criticisms in the same category seem to be based upon misapprehension of Gen. Macnaghten's speech and are omitted in the above summary.

C. S. C. R. LIG.

旧会审公廨
历史回顾

《字林西报》称
国际法庭构想荒谬

《字林西报》评论麦克纳格顿准将近期对公共租界特区法院的严厉批评，宣称对外国租界内的中国臣民及非治外法权外籍人士行使管辖权是中国国家主权不可剥夺的属性，因此中华民族决心不仅拒绝任何所谓将这些法院“国际化”的提议，而且要收回完整且不受束缚的控制权。国民新闻社在社论摘要中如是说。

社论首先回顾了租界司法管理的历史，指出中国当局（在1911年之前）既未通过条约也未在事实上放弃在租界的司法管辖权。

1912年革命

只是利用了1912年革命带来的动荡局势，租界内的外国领事当局才“篡夺”了中国的司法行政权，并任命了他们自己的中国法官。

因此，通过1926年会审公廨的移交，中国政府并未从外国当局获得任何让步，而仅仅是收回了那些违背国际法和条约规定被篡夺并非法保留的权利。

会审公廨移交

社论还惋惜道，在会审公廨移交协议进行修订时，中国政府未能收回对法院的完整且不受束缚的管辖权，反而同意了对法院权利的重要限制，例如规定附属于法院的司法警察必须从工部局提名的人选中挑选，起诉权必须保留在工部局律师手中，而法院检察官权力寥寥或毫无权力；最后，附属于法院的监狱仍由工部局当局控制。

中国领土

在提及麦克纳格顿将军在近期外国纳税人年度会议上的讲话后，社论宣称：“我们必须向麦克纳格顿将军及其他持有同样心态的外国人强调这样一个事实：上海公共租界仍然是中国领土不可分割的一部分，租界内的司法管辖权 inherent 于我们的国家主权之中。”

“此外，应强调指出，公共租界内的法院必须以对所有诉讼当事人（不论国籍）实行公平且不偏不倚的司法，以及维护总体秩序与安全为目标。外国居民不得自欺欺人地认为设立这些法院仅仅是为了外国人的利益或寻求满足外国人，也不得认为法院应当以损害他人为代价来保护此类利益。”

国际法院构想

最后，社论指出了以国际法院取代现有中国法院这一构想的荒谬性。这种制度固有的缺陷使其绝对不可行。

例如，司法管理 presupposes 存在一套统一且确定的法律。这将是哪部法律？既然外国人对中国法律不满，后者将被排除在外。如果实施任何特定国家（中国除外）的法律，难以想象其他国家的国民如何能感到满意。

此外，将外国法律适用于租界内占绝大多数的中国人口，怎能被认为是公平和公正的？如果要适用的法律仍是中国法律，那么显而易见，在管理中国法律方面，没有外国人比中国人自己更有能力。“我们完全看不出麦克纳格顿将军如何能发明出一部能让居住在租界的所有不同国籍国民都感到满意和认可的法律。”此外，“这些法院的管辖权应置于何种权威之下？中国政府？英国政府？还是工部局？”社论问道。同一类别的其他一些批评似乎基于对麦克纳格顿将军讲话的误解，在上述摘要中予以省略。

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, APRIL 22, 1932
Chairman's Speech At British Chamber Of Commerce Annual

The following is the full text of the speech of Mr. E. Calder-Marshall, chairman of the British Chamber of Commerce, at its annual meeting held yesterday:

"Probably no year since the establishment of the Republic has been so full of major problems for China as the year 1931 or rather the twelve months since our last annual meeting. In addition to communism and banditry which in themselves provided a serious problem, China has been faced with political dissensions between Nanking and Canton; flood of unprecedented extent in the Yangtse Valley; the Sino-Japanese trouble in Manchuria, and in the year the Sino-Japanese hostilities in Shanghai.

"In the early part of 1931, it appeared that with the exception of the ever present communist and bandit menaces with which the Government was trying to cope, there were prospects of peace throughout the country and hopes were raised that the Peoples Conference in May would lead to the co-ordination of national and party interests to the country's need for constructive effort, and that trade, commerce and industry in 1931 would be able to show substantial gains.

Hopes Are Dashed

"These hopes were soon dashed to the ground, for in June, Canton broke away from Nanking and a separate government independent of Nanking was established in the South. Nanking already fully committed in its campaign against the communists and bandits in Kiangsi, was unable to divert forces to combat the new element of disunion, and as Canton maintained a defensive attitude, an outbreak of hostilities was happily averted.

However, the possibility of civil war was ever present, sapping the confidence of merchants and industrialists and preventing the development that would normally have taken place.

In August the Yangtse Valley suffered one of the worst floods in the history of China—the inundation covering an area nearly equal to the size of France—and causing great loss of life and material loss which cannot be computed.

Chinese Curses To Aid

To meet this overwhelming catastrophe the Chinese mobilised all their resources—resources already strained almost to the limit—and as a result of the organisation of the National Flood Relief Commission, and the work done by it, many thousands of refugees have been saved and fed and the farmers have been helped to make a new start.

In order to meet the extraordinary expenditure incurred through this calamity the National Government authorised the collection of a surtax of 30 per cent on Customs duties up to June 30, 1932, and while this surtax it is estimated will be sufficient to cover a large part of the extraordinary flood relief expenditure. Though at first emergency relief was freely distributed, as soon as the recession of the flood permitted, relief was given in exchange for labor, employed in repairing the dykes, to a scale calculated to provide a reserve of the population.

Government Retires

One of these few great problems which confronted the country during the past year was the retirement of the late Marshal Chang Tso-lin's son, Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang, from the whole of North China. This move favored Mr. Sun Fo and the Canton group, which established a government under the leadership of Mr. Sun Fo. The government leadership of Mr. Sun Fo was short-lived, however, and after a few weeks he resigned.

Was Brought Out

On January 28th, the Sino-Japanese hostilities broke out in Shanghai. The Chinese forces, under the command of General Ting Kwan, put up a brave resistance against the Japanese forces. The fighting continued for several weeks, and although the Chinese forces were eventually forced to withdraw, they had inflicted heavy casualties on the Japanese.

The following comparative figures are given by Mr. MacEwan of the Customs Statistical Department, show a substantial decrease in Silver values of imports but while in terms of gold, the value of gross imports has been maintained, the importation of manufactured goods register a decline:

Industry Down

"Industrial development during 1931 was disappointing. In the early part of the year, the good crop prospects in the interior added to the appearance of greater stability gave confidence to industrialists and seemed to embolden upon plans for development of industry, but though some development has taken place, the Canton-Nanking split, the flood and the Manchurian crisis, have unfortunately caused the suspension of many projects which would have been beneficial to industrial development and have aided in building up the country's wealth.

Notwithstanding the heavy fall in the revenues of the Customs were affected, owing to the establishment of the new solution of duties in terms of Gold units which had a definite relation to the various foreign gold currencies. By this system China has been enabled to meet all her gold obligations based on the Customs revenues without difficulty, and though as a result of other countries coming off the gold standard the fixed ratios have had to be adjusted, in some cases, the system of collecting duties in gold units it still maintains that insuring China's gold obligations.

Though these notices were sent out by the various dealers associations, it is only fair to state that there are many of the better class buyers who, notwithstanding financial stringencies, are endeavouring to meet their obligations loyally, but unfortunately there are many others who rely upon the ineffectiveness of the District Court are leaving the importers in a bad way.

Many Meet Obligations

Though these notices were sent out by the various dealers associations, it is only fair to state that there are many of the better class buyers who, notwithstanding financial stringencies, are endeavouring to meet their obligations loyally, but unfortunately there are many others who rely upon the ineffectiveness of the District Court are leaving the importers in a bad way.

Manchurian Conflict

"The outstanding event of the year was of course the crisis in Manchuria. As this question is now the subject of investigations by the League of Nations Commission headed by Lord Lytton, it would be improper and undesirable to make any comment on the present occasion. It is to be hoped that as a result of the investigations now being made, a satisfactory solution of the problems may be reached and that the many controversial points may be settled paving the way open for the untrammelled development of this great area.

"It was but natural that the events in Manchuria should produce reactions in other parts of China, and that the people should be deeply stirred. Unfortunately, the students, showed an entire absence of discipline and disregarding the efforts being made by the leaders of the government to meet the grave crisis, injected themselves into the arena with an unbalanced enthusiasm which unquestionably added fuel to the fire and aggravated the situation.

"The inevitable boycott became in the hands of the Anti-Japanese Boycott Association a menace to law and order, for the Anti-Japanese Boycott Association disregarded alike the law, the liberty of the individual and the rights of property. One of the effects of this very active boycott was naturally an increase in trade with Great Britain due to the substitution being made for goods previously purchased in Japan, but while British trade benefited, benefits resulting from the severity of the boycott cannot be considered as satisfactory.

"As a result of the hostilities in Shanghai, trade was brought to a standstill and many dealers who had placed large orders for British goods during the Autumn of 1931, feeling that the Sino-Japanese hostilities would render it difficult if not impossible to dispose of the goods, sent cables to importers cancelling their orders regardless of their obligations and the commitments which had been entered into by the importers.

British Urges Co-operation

Though the report of the British mission which was issued last year, contains nothing new regarding the desirability of closer co-operation between British and Chinese business interests, it is hoped that the recommendations contained therein will be given careful consideration by the Chinese authorities. The mission emphasized the need for a more stable currency and a more efficient customs administration, both of which are essential for the development of trade and industry.

It is also hoped that the Chinese Government will take steps to improve the conditions of labor and to encourage the development of native industries. The mission pointed out that the present system of taxation is too heavy and that it tends to discourage investment and enterprise. It is therefore suggested that the Government should consider the possibility of reducing the tax burden and of providing more favorable conditions for business.

The mission also recommended that the Chinese Government should take steps to improve the transportation facilities and to develop the internal trade of the country. It is believed that these measures would do much to stimulate economic activity and to promote the general welfare of the people.

In conclusion, the mission expressed the hope that the Chinese Government would continue to pursue a policy of friendly co-operation with foreign powers and that it would take steps to remove the obstacles which at present hinder the development of trade and industry. It is believed that such a policy would be in the best interests of China and would contribute to the peace and prosperity of the world.

英国商会年会主席致辞

以下为英国商会主席 E. Calder-Marshall 先生在昨日举行的年度会议上发表的讲话全文：

“自中华民国成立以来，恐怕没有任何一年像1931年——或者更确切地说，是自我们上次年度会议以来的十二个月——那样充满重大问题。除了共产主义和匪患本身构成的严重问题外，中国还面临着南京与广州之间的政治分歧；长江流域发生前所未有的洪水；满洲的中日纠纷，以及本年度上海发生的中日战事。

“在1931年初，除了政府正努力应对的始终存在的共产主义和匪患威胁外，全国似乎有望实现和平，人们寄希望于5月的国民会议能够协调国家利益与党派利益，以满足国家对建设性努力的需求，并期望1931年的贸易、商业和工业能够显示出实质性的增长。

希望破灭

“这些希望很快破灭了，因为6月，广州脱离南京，南方建立了一个独立于南京的政府。南京已全力投入在江西剿共清匪的战役中，无法抽调兵力来应对这一新的分裂因素，而由于广州采取守势，幸而未爆发敌对行动。

然而，内战的可能性始终存在，这侵蚀了商人和工业家的信心，阻碍了本应正常进行的发展。

8月，长江流域遭受了中国历史上最严重的洪水之一——淹没面积几乎相当于法国的大小——造成了巨大的人员伤亡和无法估量的物质损失。

中国全力救灾

为了应对这场压倒性的灾难，中国动员了其所有资源——这些资源已经紧绷至极限——通过组织全国水灾救济委员会及其开展的工作，成千上万的难民得到了救助和供养，农民也获得了帮助以重新开始生产。

为了支付因这场灾难而产生的巨额开支，国民政府授权征收截至1932年6月30日的海关关税30%的附加税，据估计，这项附加税足以覆盖大部分额外的防洪救灾支出。虽然紧急救济物资起初是免费发放的，但一旦洪水退去允许行动，救济便改为以工代赈，用于修复堤坝，其规模旨在为人口提供储备。

政府更迭

过去一年中国家面临的少数几个重大问题之一是前张作霖元帅之子张学良元帅撤出整个华北地区。这一举动有利于孙科先生及广州派系，他们在孙科先生的领导下建立了政府。然而，孙科先生的政府领导地位短暂，几周后他便辞职了。

战事爆发

1月28日，中日战事在上海爆发。在丁官（音译）将军指挥下的中国军队对日军进行了英勇抵抗。战斗持续了数周，虽然中国军队最终被迫撤退，但他们给日军造成了重大伤亡。

工业下滑

“1931年的工业发展令人失望。年初，内地良好的收成前景加上局势看似更加稳定，增强了工业家的信心，似乎鼓励他们制定工业发展计划，但尽管发生了一些发展，广州-南京分裂、洪水和满洲危机不幸导致许多原本有利于工业发展并有助于增加国家财富的项目停滞。

尽管海关收入大幅下降，但由于建立了以金单位计算的新关税解决方案，其与各种外国金币有明确关系，因此受到影响。通过这一制度，中国得以毫无困难地履行基于海关收入的所有黄金债务，尽管由于其他国家放弃金本位制，固定比率在某些情况下不得不进行调整，但以金单位征收关税的制度仍然维持着，从而保障中国的黄金债务履行。

虽然各经销商协会发出了这些通知，但公平地说，有许多较优质的买家尽管资金紧张，仍努力忠实地履行其义务，但不幸的是，还有许多其他人依赖地方法院的无效执行，使进口商陷入困境。

许多人履行义务

虽然各经销商协会发出了这些通知，但公平地说，有许多较优质的买家尽管资金紧张，仍努力忠实地履行其义务，但不幸的是，还有许多其他人依赖地方法院的无效执行，使进口商陷入困境。

满洲冲突

“当然，本年度的突出事件是满洲危机。由于这一问题目前是由以李顿勋爵为首的国际联盟调查团进行调查的主题，在此场合发表任何评论都是不恰当且不可取的。希望随着目前进行的调查，这些问题能得到令人满意的解决，许多争议点得以平息，从而为这一广大地区的 unrestricted（不受限制）发展铺平道路。

“满洲事件在中国其他地区引起反响，民众深受触动，这是很自然的。不幸的是，学生们表现出完全缺乏纪律，无视政府领导人为应对严重危机所做的努力，以不平衡的热情介入事态，这无疑火上浇油，加剧了局势。

“不可避免的抵制运动在抗日抵制协会手中成为对法律和秩序的威胁，因为抗日抵制协会既无视法律，也无视个人自由和财产权利。这种非常活跃的抵制运动的影响之一，自然是由于取代了以前从日本购买的商品，导致与英国的贸易增加，但是，虽然英国贸易受益，但这种由严厉抵制造成的收益不能被认为是令人满意的。

“由于上海的战事，贸易陷入停顿，许多在1931年秋季订购了大量英国货物的经销商，认为中日战事将使处理这些货物变得困难甚至不可能，不顾其义务和进口商已作出的承诺，发电报给进口商取消订单。

英国敦促合作

虽然去年发布的英国代表团报告在英中商业利益之间加强合作的必要性方面没有提出新内容，但希望其中包含的建议能得到中国当局的认真考虑。该代表团强调了更稳定的货币和更高效的海关管理的必要性，这两者对于贸易和工业的发展都至关重要。

也希望中国政府采取措施改善劳动条件并鼓励民族工业的发展。代表团指出，目前的税收制度过重，倾向于抑制投资和创业精神。因此建议政府考虑减轻税收负担并为商业提供更有利的条件。

代表团还建议中国政府采取措施改善交通设施并发展国内贸易。相信这些措施将极大地刺激经济活动并促进人民的普遍福利。

最后，代表团表示希望中国政府将继续推行与外国列强友好合作的政策，并采取措施消除目前阻碍贸易和工业发展的障碍。相信这样的政策符合中国的最大利益，并将有助于世界的和平与繁荣。”

This ferry when in operation should
greatly facilitate the transport of cargo
to and from the North and should prove
of the greatest value to trade and a
benefit alike to Nanking-Shanghai and
Tientsin-Pukow railways.

While on the subject of railways it
is pertinent to state that the unpaid
railway debts which have been outstand-
ing for years, still remain unpaid. Con-
sidering that these debts were incurred for
materials and rolling stock required for
the maintenance of the railways, they
should have been a first charge on the
revenues of the railways to which they
were supplied, it is a standing reproach
to the Ministry of Railways that no effort
should have been made to meet these
obligations.

It is realized that the Government has
many calls on its resources and that the
constant drain caused by civil wars may
well account for the inability of the
Government to pay the debts. There
would, however, appear to be no reason
why the Ministry of Railways should not
prepare a scheme for funding the debts,
making provision for payment of interest
and amortization from the revenues of
the railways, which properly managed
should be sufficient.

Credit China's Problem

While the rehabilitation of China's rail-
ways can and will be provided for in
part by loans from indemnity funds, the
restoration of China's credit must be a
matter for China. As long as these debts
remain as they are, a reproach to China's
railway administration, it cannot be
anticipated that the financial facilities so
much needed by China will be readily
forthcoming.

Though the financial stringency
brought about by the Sino-Japanese
troubles in Shanghai, did not occur until
this year, the stagnation in trade and
financial chaos resulting from the limited
functioning of the native banks is a matter
of the most serious concern to a commer-
cial centre such as Shanghai, and calls
for the serious consideration of mer-
chants and bankers who are dependent
upon the free flow of cash.

As the nerve center of China's finance,
any disorganization of the banking system
of the port must inevitably have wide-
spread and disastrous reactions particu-
larly in North and Central China.

Though the native banks are now
functioning more normally, the temporary
partial suspension during February and
March gave a severe shock to the com-
mercial community, and to the confidence
that they had hitherto reposed in the
native bank orders. It is of course true
that native banks which carry the main
burden of commerce and trade for the
Chinese in Shanghai and the interior, have
had to meet a combination of circum-
stances, viz: the flood in the Yangtze
area, the absorption of large amounts on
account of the boycott,—the value of
"frozen" Japanese cargo in Shanghai
alone being estimated at T$30,000,000—and
the natural dislocation and losses brought
about by the local hostilities, but at the
same time it is felt that some means
should be adopted by the native banks
which would lead to greater stability at
times of crisis and avoid the necessity
of adopting such drastic measures as the
issue of inconvertible bank orders, which
for a time brought all trade to a standstill.
The modern style Chinese bankers have
between them established a reserve bank
for the purpose of meeting such crisis as
that through which we have just passed,
and it would seem desirable for the guild
banks to adopt similar means for providing
the necessary stability.

Tariff Not Affected Trade

The new import tariff which came
into effect February 1, 1931 was referred
to in the last annual report. Though
in some classifications the increases ap-
pear unduly heavy, the imposition of the
higher tariff has not seriously affected the
general import trade.

The revised export tariff designed to
yield an effective 7½ per cent duty on
all exports became operative in June. In
connection with this your committee en-
deavored to make arrangements so that
bona fide purchases made prior to the
promulgation of the new tariff but not
shipped until after June might to ex-
empted from payment of the increase in
duty, but their efforts were without avail.

In connection with export duties it
appears to your committee that in view
of the adverse trade balance, it would
be to the advantage of China were export
duties entirely abolished. Such action
should result in greatly increased exports
and by reducing the adverse trade balance
more than compensate for the loss of
revenues that would result.

It has been the policy of the Ministry
of Finance, under Mr. T. V. Soong, to
reduce the number of national taxes and
consolidate such taxation in as few ad-
ministrations as possible.

Suggests Merging

The final logical development should
be the merging of all tax services into
Customs, Salt and Internal Revenue Ad-
ministrations. Though this consolidation
has not yet been completed, progress has
been made which if continued should lead
to considerable simplification and economy
and benefit trade, commerce and industry.
Could similar steps be taken with regard
to provincial and local taxation, great
savings in higher trade and progressive
very substantial improvement should
become apparent in the trade balance of
the country.

"As Mr. Soong pointed out in his
last financial report, there is urgent
need of co-ordination of effort and
reconstruction, and in this connection
it is of interest to record that
the past year has witnessed definite
efforts towards reconstruction according to
pre-arranged plan.

Before turning to the routine work
of the chamber, I would like to refer
to the very able annual report recently
made by Mr. Chang Kin Ngau, managing
director of the Bank of China.

Mr. Chang points out that notwith-
standing the material progress made in
the world which tends to bind the na-
tions more closely together, people still
think in terms of narrow nationalism much
as they did a century ago; that this
narrow point of view is largely the cause
of the world crisis; that there must be
a change in our way of thinking.

Cast Off Jealousies

In summing up, he says, "We must
put aside jealousies, suspicions and self-
complacency and abandon the habits of
words in favor of action. Then internal
conditions will improve, domestic warfare
will be avoided and the change in the

thought and action of our people will result
in a greater measure of co-operation with
other nations. Misunderstanding between
China and the other powers will disappear
and we shall be able to lend a hand in
establishing peace not only in the Far
East but throughout the world. I there-
fore venture to say that there must be
a change in our way of thinking."

The underlying thought of Mr. Chang's
remarks is that in view of the interna-
tional interdependence of the world, to
secure the best results for all, there must
be whole-hearted co-operation, a working
together for the common good.

We as a chamber are in agreement
and sympathy with what Mr. Chang has
expressed but in many cases our efforts
to assist in developing the trade, com-
merce and industry of this city, and of
the country have been hindered by ob-
structive acts and restrictive laws.

China has men with culture and ability,
who have vision and the power to see
through. When, however, we think of
the difficult problems, economic, financial
and political, both national and interna-
tional, with which the countries of the
West are struggling and then consider
the problems that confront this country,
with her vast areas, and her enormous
heterogeneous population, speaking many
dialects, we should be generous and
understanding in our helpfulness and
considerate and constructive in our criti-
cisms.

The Language School

Turning now to the internal workings
of the chamber. One of the most im-
portant departments of the chamber is
the Language School. Each year it be-
comes increasingly evident that a sound
knowledge of the Chinese language both
written and colloquial is necessary for
those who expect to maintain and expand
their trade in China. In correspondence
with Chinese authorities the use of the
Chinese language is now usually insisted
upon and unless one is willing to place
oneself unreservedly in the hands and at
the mercy of a Chinese interpreter, a
knowledge of the language is essential if
one may at least check the
translations that are made.

Though at every annual meeting for
several years past employers have been
urged to insist upon their juniors study-
ing the Chinese language, I make no
apology for once again emphasizing the
importance of a sound knowledge of
Chinese.

The school has been established many
years and has gained a well deserved re-
putation for thoroughness. The work done
by its principal, Mr. John S. Lee, has
been highly commended by the examiners,
all of whom are British consular officials.
Full particulars of the curriculum, the
full course extends over four years, can
be obtained from the secretary.

Shorthand and Typewriting
Examinations

For many years past commercial ex-
aminations have been held in Shanghai
by the British Chamber of Commerce
acting as local centre of the Education
Department of the London Chamber of
Commerce. About a year ago, your com-
mittee decided that the time was opportune
to form its own education department.
This was done on February 5, 1931. Its
activities were confined to shorthand and
typewriting. The first examinations were
held in May of last year and the second
in November. These examinations are
not intended for beginners, and they
are open to persons of both sexes and
of all nationalities. The goal aimed at
is increased efficiency. The examinations
are a test not only of the candidates'
knowledge of shorthand and typewriting,
but of their general intelligence and
general knowledge of business phrases.
The examinations have attracted a type
of candidate determined to equip herself
thoroughly for any stenographic-secretarial
position. Any candidate passing the
chamber's examinations may be reasonably
sure of having qualified for a responsible
position and any prospective employer
may also be reasonably sure of having
obtained an employee a little above the
average.

I would urge members, when they are
in need of employees whose qualifications
are within the scope of our examinations,
to make enquiries at the chamber's offices
to see if they have passed our examina-
tions. By doing so, they will be pro-
tecting themselves and doing a service
to those who have been keen enough to
sit and pass a difficult but, from the
employer's point of view, necessary test.

Chamber's Publications

A second volume of the treaties con-
cluded by China with the foreign Powers
was issued by the Chamber at the end
of the year. Two new volumes, Nos. 6
and 7, containing translations of laws
and regulations issued by the Nanking
Government were also published. The
demand for these publications justifies the
time spent in compiling them and in
careful translation.

Arbitrations and Surveys

The number of arbitrations and sur-
veys conducted by the chamber last year
was only 18 as compared with 30 in 1930.
On many occasions, however, the aid of
the Chamber has been sought by Chinese
dealers in clearing up points of difficulty
that have arisen between themselves and
their suppliers.

Trade Enquiries

As in past years, the time of the
Staff has been fully occupied dealing with
trade enquiries. These come from the
parts of the world and are invariably
answered as fully as possible, whether it
be requests for statistics, enquiries in re-
gard to commodities, requests for agencies
in Shanghai or offers to act as agents.
Such of these enquiries as are considered
of interests to members are passed on
by means of circular letters. Many
valuable connections have been formed in
this way.

Employment Department

The Employment Department continues
active. During the year under review
over 172 applicants were entered on the
register. I am glad to say that positions

have been found for a large number,
though unfortunately, owing to the dif-
ficult times through which we have been
passing, it has not been too easy to
place many of them. I would ask mem-
bers, when vacancies occur in their offices,
to bear in mind that the chamber has
an employment register. Every care is
taken, wherever possible to assess the
right person to fill a position.

The thanks of the chamber are due
to Mr. J. F. Breen, our consul-general,
who has at all times been willing to give
us assistance and advice, and to Mr. H.
J. Brett, commercial counselor of Legation,
who has just retired from official
life.

Mr. Brett has been intimately associated
with the chamber for the past eleven
years, and the Chamber and the British
commercial community in Shanghai owe
much to his efficient service and sound
advice and help, and I want to take this
opportunity of expressing our individual
and collective appreciation of the work
done by him on behalf of British interests
in China.

While regretting Mr. Brett's departure,
we welcome Mr. Louis Beale who has just
taken up his duties as commercial coun-
selor. The experience that Mr. Beale
brings with him from other parts of the
world will undoubtedly prove advantageous
to British trade, and we hope that as
a result of his efforts trade between Great
Britain and China will expand.

The thanks of the chamber are also
due to the members of the sub-committees
who have given so generously of their
services, and also to the secretary, assis-
tant secretary, and staff for their loyal
work and co-operation. This year I
particularly wish to mention our assistant
secretary, Miss Ayrton, who during the
absence of the secretary on leave carried
on the work most efficiently.

Statement Of Accounts

In spite of the unprecedented increase
in expenditure caused through the fall
in exchange, and the somewhat abnormal
amount spent on telegrams during the
year, it is gratifying to note that the
working account shows a credit balance
of T$52.91.

The financial report and statement of
accounts for 1931 is in your hands and
it is not therefore necessary for me to
deal more fully with them.

I have now pleasure in moving the
adoption of the report and accounts for
the year ending December 31, 1931.

南京至浦口的火车轮渡。
该轮渡一旦投入运营，将极大便利往返华北的货物运输，并被证明对贸易具有极大价值，同时惠及京沪铁路和津浦铁路。

在谈及铁路之际，有必要指出，多年来悬而未决的铁路债务仍未偿还。鉴于这些债务是因维持铁路所需的材料和机车车辆而产生的，它们本应作为向其提供物资的铁路收入的首要扣款项；铁道部未作出任何努力来履行这些义务，实为一种持续的耻辱。

人们认识到，政府资源面临诸多需求，内战造成的持续消耗很可能解释了政府无力偿债的原因。然而，似乎没有理由说明铁道部为何不制定一项债务基金化方案，从铁路收入中拨付款项以支付利息和本金摊销，若管理得当，这些收入应当是充足的。

中国的信用问题

虽然中国铁路的复兴可以且将在部分程度上通过赔款基金的贷款来解决，但中国信用的恢复必须由中国自己负责。只要这些债务依然如故，成为中国铁路行政管理的污点，就不能指望中国迫切需要的金融便利会轻易到来。

尽管由上海中日纠纷引发的财政紧缩直到今年才发生，但因钱庄运作受限而导致的贸易停滞和金融混乱，是像上海这样的商业中心最为严重关切的问题，需要依赖现金自由流动的商人和银行家认真考虑。

作为中国金融的神经中枢，该口岸银行体系的任何紊乱都必然会产生广泛且灾难性的反响，尤其是在华北和华中的地区。

虽然钱庄目前运作已较为正常，但二、三月份的暂时部分停业给商界带来了严重冲击，也打击了他们此前对钱庄庄票所持有的信心。诚然，承担着上海及内地华人商业贸易主要负担的钱庄，不得不应对一系列情况，即：长江流域的水灾、因抵制运动而吸收的大量资金——仅在上海，“冻结”的日本货物价值估计就达关平银3,000万两——以及当地敌对行动造成的自然脱节和损失。但与此同时，人们认为钱庄应采取某些措施，以便在危机时刻带来更大的稳定性，避免采取发行不可兑换庄票等剧烈手段，这种做法曾一度使所有贸易陷入停顿。现代式样的华资银行家之间已建立了一家储备银行，旨在应对我们刚刚经历的这类危机，同业公会银行（guild banks）似乎也应采取类似手段，以提供必要的稳定性。

关税未影响贸易

上一份年度报告中提到了1931年2月1日生效的新进口关税。尽管在某些分类中增幅显得过重，但征收较高关税并未严重影响整体进口贸易。

旨在对所有出口商品征收有效7.5%税率的修订后出口关税于六月生效。就此，本委员会努力做出安排，以便在新关税颁布之前但在六月之后装运的真实购买行为能够免除增加的税款，但其努力未果。

关于出口税，本委员会认为，鉴于贸易逆差，如果完全取消出口税，将有利于中国。此举应导致出口大幅增加，并通过减少贸易逆差，充分补偿由此造成的财政收入损失。

在宋子文先生领导下，财政部的政策一直是减少国家税种，并尽可能将此类税收合并到少数几个管理机构中。

建议合并

最终合乎逻辑的发展应是将所有税务服务合并到海关、盐务和统税管理局中。虽然这一整合尚未完成，但已取得进展，若继续下去，应能带来相当大的简化和节约，并惠及贸易、商业和工业。如果在省和地方税收方面也能采取类似步骤，高层贸易将大幅节省，国家的贸易平衡状况也将出现非常显著的改善。

“正如宋先生在最近的财政报告中指出的那样，迫切需要进行协调努力和重建，在此方面，值得注意的是，过去一年见证了按照预定计划进行重建的明确努力。

在转向商会的日常工作之前，我想提及中国银行总经理张嘉璈先生最近发表的极具见地的年度报告。

张先生指出，尽管世界在物质上取得了进步，倾向于使各国联系更加紧密，但人们的思维仍然像一百年前那样局限于狭隘的民族主义；这种狭隘的观点很大程度上是世界危机的原因；我们的思维方式必须改变。

摒弃嫉妒

他在总结时说：“我们必须放下嫉妒、猜疑和自满，放弃空谈的习惯而 favor 行动。这样，内部状况将会改善，国内战争将会避免，我国人民思想和行为的改变将导致与其他国家更大程度的合作。中国与其他列强之间的误解将会消失，我们将能够协助不仅在远东，而且在全世界建立和平。因此，我冒昧地说，我们的思维方式必须改变。”

张先生言论的核心思想是，鉴于世界的国际相互依赖性，为了为所有人争取最佳结果，必须进行全心全意的合作，为共同利益共同努力。

作为商会，我们赞同并同情张先生所表达的观点，但在许多情况下，我们协助发展本市及全国贸易、商业和工业的努力受到了阻碍性行为和限制性法律的妨碍。

中国拥有有文化、有能力、有远见和洞察力的人才。然而，当我们想到西方国家正在挣扎的经济、金融和政治难题，无论是国内的还是国际的，再考虑到这个幅员辽阔、人口众多且异质、讲多种方言的国家所面临的问题时，我们在提供帮助时应慷慨且具理解力，在批评时应体贴且具有建设性。

语言学校

现在转向商会的内部运作。商会最重要的部门之一是语言学校。每年越来越明显的是，对于那些希望在中国维持和扩大贸易的人来说，扎实的中文书面和口语知识是必要的。在与中方当局通信时，现在通常坚持使用中文，除非一个人愿意将自己完全置于中文译员的手中和摆布之下，否则掌握语言是必不可少的，至少可以核对所做的翻译。

尽管在过去几年的每次年会上，雇主都被敦促坚持要求其初级职员学习中文，但我再次强调扎实掌握中文的重要性，这无需道歉。

该校已成立多年，并因其严谨性赢得了应有的声誉。其校长李约翰（John S. Lee，音译）先生的工作受到了考官的高度赞扬，所有考官均为英国领事官员。课程的全部详情，完整课程为期四年，可向秘书索取。

速记和打字考试

多年来，商业考试一直由英国商会作为伦敦商会教育部的地方中心在上海举行。大约一年前，本委员会决定时机成熟，成立自己的教育部。此事于1931年2月5日完成。其活动限于速记和打字。第一次考试于去年五月举行，第二次于十一月举行。这些考试并非针对初学者，而是面向所有性别和国籍的人士。其目标是提高效率。这些考试不仅测试候选人的速记和打字知识，还测试其一般智力和对商业短语的一般了解。这些考试吸引了一类决心为任何 stenographic-secretarial（速记-秘书）职位做好充分准备的候选人。任何通过商会考试的候选人都可以有把握地认为自己已具备担任重要职位的资格，任何潜在雇主也可以有把握地认为已获得一名略高于平均水平的员工。

我敦促会员在需要 qualifications（资格）在我们考试范围内的员工时，向商会办公室查询，看看他们是否通过了我们的考试。这样做，他们既保护了自己，也为那些敏锐到足以参加并通过一项困难但从雇主角度来看必要的测试的人提供了服务。

商会出版物

商会于年底发行了中国与各外国列强签订的条约第二卷。还出版了两本新卷，第6和第7卷，包含南京政府颁布的法律和法规的译文。对这些出版物的需求证明了在编纂和仔细翻译上所花费的时间是合理的。

仲裁与调查

去年商会进行的仲裁和调查数量仅为18起，而1930年为30起。然而，在许多场合，中国商人在清理其与供应商之间出现的难点时，曾寻求商会的帮助。

贸易咨询

与往年一样，工作人员的时间完全用于处理贸易咨询。这些咨询来自世界各地，并且总是尽可能全面地予以答复，无论是请求统计数据、询问商品、请求在上海的代理机构，还是提议担任代理。其中被认为对会员有兴趣的咨询，会通过通函转发。通过这种方式建立了许多有价值的联系。

就业部

就业部继续保持活跃。在回顾年度内，登记册上登记了超过172名申请人。我很高兴地说，已为许多人找到了职位，尽管不幸的是，由于我们经历的艰难时期，安置许多人并非易事。我请会员在其办公室出现空缺时，记住商会设有就业登记册。在可能的情况下，我们会格外小心地评估合适的人选以填补职位。

商会感谢我们的总领事 J. F. Breen 先生，他随时愿意给予我们协助和建议；并感谢公使馆商务参赞 H. J. Brett 先生，他刚刚从官场退休。

Brett 先生在过去十一年中与商会关系密切，商会和上海的英国商界得益于他高效的服务、明智的建议和帮助，我想借此机会表达我们对他在华代表英国利益所做工作的个人和集体赞赏。

在对 Brett 先生的离去表示遗憾的同时，我们欢迎刚刚上任担任商务参赞的 Louis Beale 先生。Beale 先生从世界其他地区带来的经验无疑将有利于英国贸易，我们希望在他的努力下，英中贸易得以扩展。

商会还要感谢各小组委员会成员，他们慷慨地提供服务；并感谢秘书、助理秘书和工作人员的忠诚工作与合作。今年我特别想提及我们的助理秘书 Ayrton 小姐，她在秘书休假期间非常高效地承担了工作。

账目声明

尽管由于汇率下跌导致支出空前增加，以及本年度电报费用 somewhat abnormal（略显异常），但令人欣慰的是，往来账户显示贷方余额为关平银52.91两。

1931年的财务报告和账目声明已在各位手中，因此我不必更详细地讨论它们。

我现在愉快地动议通过截至1931年12月31日的年度报告和账目。

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / REGISTRY / D 3517 / 21. 4. 32.）

Shanghai District Court
Officials Submit Reply
To Chairman's Statement

Claim Made That Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten Did Not
Fully Understand Power Of Court; Criticism
Not In Agreement With Facts

ANTI-JAPANESE BOYCOTT CASES DEALT
WITH ACCORDING TO LAW

Claiming that Brig.-Gen. E. B. Macnaghten, retired
Chairman of the Shanghai Municipal Council, did not fully
understand the power of the Shanghai District Court when
he criticised its functioning, Mr. C. Wan, Registrar of the
Court, has submitted a reply to the criticism on behalf of
the Court officials. It will be recalled that General Mac-
naghten scathingly referred to the administration of the
Court in his annual speech to ratepayers. The failure of
the Court to mete adequate punishment to offenders charged
with anti-Japanese activities was held responsible for their
intensification in Shanghai and one of the contributory
causes of the recent Sino-Japanese hostilities. The Court's
reply to these charges follows:

After reading the criticisms of
the Shanghai Special District
Court, made by Brig.-Gen.
Macnaghten, retiring chairman of
the Shanghai Municipal Council,
in his report before the annual
meeting of foreign tax-payers and
published in the newspapers on the
14th of this month, one feels that
Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten did not
fully understand the power of the
Court and that the cases he cited
in support of his criticisms were
not quite in agreement with actual
facts. In order to clear up any
possible misunderstanding on the
part of the foreign community, we
offer the following explanation:
In the first place, the question
whether the patriotic movement of
the people should be prohibited or
not comes with the jurisdiction of
the executive power with which
the court has no right to interfere.
We are not aware that there is
any law court in any civilized
country that can compel the peo-
ple to buy or refrain from buying
goods against their own will.
Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten did not,
therefore, understand the position
of the Court when he said that the
court was prejudiced against the
anti-Japanese movement. Further-
more, according to the law of this
country, cases can be tried only
when they are properly brought
before the Court. Since the 18th
of September last year, only three
cases with regard to the anti-Jap-
anese movement have been brought
before the Court by the Municipal
Council, and they were all dealt
with according to law. Individual
opinion might, of course, differ as
to what evidence should be relied
upon and what reasons applied in
the particular case, but admitted-
ly the Court had independent discre-
tion in all these matters. If the
judgment was thought wrong, the
party dissatisfied could have the
remedy of appeal. How then, can
it be said that the Court was pre-
judiced, merely because subjec-
tively Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten did
not agree with one of its judg-
ments?
Besides these three cases, there
were no other cases in connection

with the anti-Japanese movement
brought before the Court either
by the Municipal Council or by the
private individual.
Seizure Of Goods
In Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten's re-
port it was further alleged that
Japanese goods to the value of more
than $600,000, and belonging to
Chinese, were feloniously seized,
a considerable part of which were
sold and the proceeds criminally
appropriated and that a large
number of the so-called traitorous
Chinese were illegally arrested and
detained in the Temple of Heaven
and other places. But the Court
was never called upon to decide
these matters and we are not in a
position to say whether the alleged
offences ever happened or not.
So far as responsibility is concern-
ed, it should be mentioned that
the power of the procurators is
by the terms of the Agreement
confined to offences provided from
article 103 to 186 of the criminal
code. That being the case, and
assuming the alleged seizure of
goods and illegal arrests were
true, the responsibility to bring
charges did not lie with the pro-
curators.
Now that Brig.-Gen. Macnagh-
ten blamed the Court for having
turned a blind eye and deaf ear
clearly shows that he did not
understand the powers of the
Court. The further statement
that the attitude of the Court
with regard to offences connected
with the Japanese boycott and
other activities was undoubtedly
one of the contributory factors in
the accumulative causes which led
to actual warfare between the Chin-
ese and Japanese military authori-
ties is nothing but misunderstand-
ing.
In the seconds place, it should
be noticed also, that the number
of civil cases received by the
Court greatly exceeds that in the
former Provisional Court, and the
procedure thereof has also become
far more complicated. Since Pre-
sident Chau assumed office, great
efforts have been made toward im-
provement of the Court. As to the
general dissatisfaction with the
Court also mentioned in Mr.
Macnaghten's report, no specific
facts were alleged and so no more
explanation is necessary.

（批：Jule / 975 / 20.4.32）

上海特区地方法院
官员提交答复
回应总董声明

声称麦克纳格顿准将并未
充分理解法院的权力；批评
与事实不符

依法处理抵制日货案件

上海特区地方法院书记官万先生代表法院官员提交了一份对批评的答复，声称上海公共租界工部局前总董E. B. 麦克纳格顿（E. B. Macnaghten）准将在批评法院运作时，并未充分理解上海特区地方法院的权力。人们还记得，麦克纳格顿将军在向纳税人发表的年度演说中，曾严厉指责法院的行政管理。法院未能对涉嫌从事反日活动的不法分子施以适当的惩罚，被认为导致了此类活动在上海的加剧，并成为最近中日敌对行动的促成因素之一。法院对这些指控的答复如下：

在阅读了上海公共租界工部局卸任总董麦克纳格顿准将在外国纳税人年度会议上的报告中所作的、并于本月14日见诸报端的对上海特区地方法院的批评后，我们感到麦克纳格顿准将并未充分理解法院的权力，且他引用来支持其批评的案件与实际情况并不完全相符。为了消除外侨社区可能存在的任何误解，我们提供以下解释：

首先，是否应当禁止民众的爱国运动，属于行政权力的管辖范围，法院无权干涉。我们不知道在任何文明国家中，有任何法院可以强迫民众违背自身意愿购买或不购买商品。因此，当麦克纳格顿准将称法院对反日运动持有偏见时，他并不了解法院的立场。此外，根据本国法律，只有当案件被正式提交至法院时，方可进行审理。自去年9月18日以来，工部局仅向法院提交了三起与反日运动有关的案件，且均依法处理。当然，对于在具体案件中应采信何种证据以及适用何种理由，个人意见或许会有所不同，但无可否认，法院在所有这些事项上拥有独立的裁量权。如果判决被认为有误，不服的一方可以通过上诉寻求救济。那么，仅仅因为麦克纳格顿准将主观上不同意其中一项判决，怎能说法院存有偏见呢？

除这三起案件外，无论是工部局还是私人个体，均未向法院提起其他与反日运动有关的案件。

货物扣押

在麦克纳格顿准将的报告中，还指控价值超过60万美元、属于中国人的日货被非法劫掠，其中相当一部分被出售，所得款项被犯罪性地侵吞，且大量所谓的“汉奸”被非法逮捕并拘禁在天坛及其他地方。但法院从未被要求裁决这些事项，我们也无法断定上述指控的罪行是否确实发生。就责任而言，需要提及的是，根据协定条款，检察官的权力仅限于刑法典第103条至第186条规定的罪行。既然如此，假设上述货物扣押和非法逮捕属实，提起公诉的责任也不在于检察官。

如今，麦克纳格顿准将指责法院视而不见、充耳不闻，这清楚地表明他并不了解法院的权力。他进一步声称，法院在与抵制日货及其他活动有关罪行上的态度，无疑是导致中日军事当局之间爆发实际战争的各种累积原因中的促成因素之一，这纯属误解。

其次，还应注意，法院受理的民事案件数量大大超过了以前的临时法院，且诉讼程序也变得更为复杂。自周院长就职以来，为改善法院工作已做出巨大努力。至于麦克纳格顿先生报告中提到的对法院的普遍不满，由于未列举具体事实，故无需更多解释。

（批：Jule / 975 / 32.4.20）

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, APRIL 17, 1932

REALITIES
The criticisms which have been levelled against the speech of the late Chairman of the Shanghai Municipal Council, delivered at the annual meeting of ratepayers on Wednesday, illustrate the failure of our Chinese friends to distinguish between the powers and the duties of the Council. Brigadier-General Macnaghten has been taken to task because, in the course of his review of recent events, he saw fit to lament the failure of the District Courts to dispense even-handed justice while, at the same time, he avoided passing strictures upon Japanese naval and military forces which took action at the end of January and so precipitated the crisis through which we have not yet wholly passed. According to the critics, it would appear as though the Council failed to take action which lay within its power to prevent the Japanese from acting in the way they did, whereas in point of fact the Council possessed no such power and has striven to make that abundantly clear. The Council is not a State—it possesses no army or navy; it administers an area that is dependent for its protection from outside dangers upon a group of international Powers. If, as has happened, one of those Powers, through its failure to secure justice and protection for its nationals from China and the Chinese, sees fit to act on its own in a coercive way, the Council is obviously helpless to interfere. If any interference at all had been considered justified or politic, then, obviously, it had to come from among the other Powers whose Consular and military representatives are entitled to a voice in matters affecting the defence of the Settlement. The Municipal Council is concerned wholly with the preservation of law and order within the Settlement boundaries, with the work of policing, the safeguarding of health, and the provision of municipal amenities. And it strove valiantly through the worrying days of February and March to carry out the whole of its functions. It is not within the scope of the Council's activities to criticize or condemn (or praise) the action which the Japanese authorities saw fit to take. That is a matter for other tribunals. All that the Council could do was to co-operate in the schemes of the Defence Committee and to work for the care and protection of those who resided within the borders of its territory. We think it would be more fitting for Chinese critics to make grateful acknowledgment of the tremendous amount of work and thought which was put into that essential task, than it is to carp about a failure that was no failure at all. Brig.-General Macnaghten has been accused of one-sidedness; it is a foolish charge that rebounds and settles upon those who make it.
With regard to the failure of the District Courts, there is not

the slightest doubt that the absence of fair treatment was a direct contributory factor to the intensification of feeling which led to the final clash. There is no need for us to recapitulate all the well-known facts of this aspect of the matter, for they have been generally recognized by all neutral parties here—American, British, French and others. The work of the Municipal Police Force was, in many cases, rendered useless. Theft, illegal imprisonment by unauthorized persons, and extortion all went unpunished because of a parrot-cry of "patriotism" that was used simply as a cloak. We sincerely believe that if the anti-Japanese boycott had been kept confined to a no-buying movement and had not grown into an officially condoned contempt for law and personal property rights (plus unpunished assaults on Japanese residents) there would have been no Shanghai incident. It was not a Municipal function that broke down —it was the functioning of the Courts. And, as a direct consequence, there was intense acerbation of feeling which led first to stern demands by Japan and then to action. When Chinese leaders and writers to-day set out to defend in the name of patriotism all that took place prior to January 28 they betray a woeful inability to recognize past errors and offer a very gloomy prospect for the future.
In speaking of that future, General Macnaghten stated that no Shanghai problem can be permanently solved which does not take into consideration Chinese as well as foreign interests, and with that excellent dictum we heartily agree. But it needs to be pointed out that it is to the interest of all to see established here trustworthy and honest Courts of Justice. In the minds of a good many Chinese it is thought to be "anti-Chinese" to suggest that any change should be made in the status or composition of the District Courts, but that is a narrow and illogical view. It is comparable to suggesting that they are wholly satisfactory, which they notoriously are not. China has decided just recently to send more naval cadets to Great Britain to learn the arts of naval science. There is here no loss of precious "face" or political prestige in not pretending that China has nothing to learn; it would be a logical corollary to admit that Chinese jurists need help and instruction from the West just as much as executive officers of the navy which it is hoped to build up. Co-operation for mutual benefit should be China's aim in administration as well as in any other branch of endeavour, and especially does this apply in and around Shanghai where mutual interests are so intertwined and involved. The suggestion that foreign jurists should assist Chinese is not derogatory to China; it is but a frank recognition of realities. On that plane, and no other, must this problem be considered.

（批：3547. 18.4.32.）
（手写批注：Reg. J. Macnaghten 18:4-33）

《上海星期日报》，1932年4月17日

现实

针对上海公共租界工部局前总董在周三纳税人年度会议上所作演说提出的批评，说明我们的中国朋友未能区分工部局的权力与职责。麦克纳格顿准将受到责难，是因为他在回顾近期事件时，认为有必要哀叹特区法院未能实行公正的司法，同时却避免对一月底采取行动从而引发我们尚未完全度过的危机的日本海陆军部队进行严厉谴责。根据批评者的说法，似乎工部局未能采取其权力范围内可防止日本人如此行事的行动，而事实上工部局并无此种权力，并一直努力使这一点变得十分清楚。工部局不是一个国家——它没有军队或海军；它管理的区域依赖于一组国际列强来保护其免受外部危险。如果像已经发生的那样，其中一个列强因未能从中国及中国人那里为其国民获得正义和保护，而认为有必要单独采取强制行动，工部局显然无力干涉。如果认为任何干涉是正当或明智的，那么显然，这种干涉必须来自其他列强，其领事和军事代表有权在对租界防务有影响的事项上发表意见。工部局完全关注于维持租界边界内的法律和秩序、警务工作、健康保障以及提供市政便利设施。在二月和三月那些令人担忧的日子里，工部局英勇地努力履行其全部职能。批评或谴责（或赞扬）日本当局认为有必要采取的行动，不在工部局的活动范围之内。那是其他法庭的事。工部局所能做的一切，就是配合防卫委员会的计划，并为居住在其领土边界内的人们提供照料和保护。我们认为，中国批评家更适宜对投入这一基本任务的大量工作和思考表示感激，而不是去挑剔一个根本不算失败的失败。麦克纳格顿准将被指责有片面性；这是一个愚蠢的指控，反而反弹并落在提出指控的人身上。

关于特区法院的失职，毫无疑问，缺乏公平待遇是直接促成导致最终冲突的情绪激化的因素。我们无需重述这方面众所周知的所有事实，因为这里的各方中立人士——美国人、英国人、法国人及其他人士——已普遍承认。在许多情况下，公共租界巡捕房的工作变得徒劳无功。盗窃、未经授权人员的非法监禁以及勒索均未受惩罚，因为“爱国主义”的鹦鹉学舌般的喊叫仅仅被用作掩护。我们真诚地相信，如果抵制日货运动仅限于不购买运动，而没有演变成官方纵容的对法律和个人财产权的蔑视（加上对日本居民的袭击不受惩罚），就不会有上海事变。崩溃的不是市政职能，而是法院的运作。作为直接后果，情绪剧烈恶化，首先导致日本的强硬要求，随后导致行动。当今中国领导人和作家以爱国主义的名义为1月28日之前发生的一切进行辩护时，暴露出他们可悲地无法认识过去的错误，并为未来提供了非常黯淡的前景。

在谈到未来时，麦克纳格顿将军指出，任何不考虑中国和外国利益的上海问题都无法得到永久解决，我们衷心同意这一极好的格言。但需要指出的是，在此建立值得信赖和诚实的司法法院符合所有人的利益。在许多中国人的心目中，有人建议改变特区法院的地位或组成被视为“反华”，但这是一种狭隘且不合逻辑的观点。这相当于暗示它们完全令人满意，而众所周知事实并非如此。中国最近决定派遣更多海军学员前往英国学习海军科学艺术。在这里，不假装中国没有什么可学的，并不会损失宝贵的“面子”或政治声望；承认中国法学家需要西方的帮助和指导，就像希望建立的海军行政官员需要帮助和指导一样，是一个合乎逻辑的推论。互利合作应是中国在行政管理以及任何其他努力领域的目标，尤其适用于上海及其周边地区，因为那里的相互利益如此交织和复杂。建议外国法学家协助中国并非贬低中国；这只是对现实的坦率承认。必须在这一层面，而非其他层面，来考虑这个问题。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, MONDAY, APRIL 18, 1932

GEN. MacNAGHTEN
CRITICISED

Special District Court
Explains Position

ALLEGED LACK OF
UNDERSTANDING

Alleging that Brigadier-General E. B. Macnaghten showed a lack of understanding of the exact position of the Shanghai Special District Court when he made certain remarks concerning that institution at the annual meeting of ratepayers last Wednesday, the Secretariat of the Court has addressed the following letter to the various Chinese newspapers:—
“In connection with the article published in the various vernacular newspapers on April 14 on statements made by Brigadier-General Macnaghten, former Chairman of the Shanghai Municipal Council, criticising this Court at the annual meeting of the foreign ratepayers, we offer the following explanation to avoid public misunderstandings because the former Chairman of the Council does not fully understand the competency of this Court, so what he reported does not coincide with the real facts.
“It must not be forgotten that the question, whether the people’s patriotic movement should be banned or not, comes within the jurisdiction of administrative authorities. It is impossible for the Court to exceed its limits. That General Macnaghten should have stated that the Court took issue with the anti-Japanese movement is due to his lack of understanding the Court’s exact position. Since September 18, 1931, three cases have been filed in the Court by the Shanghai Municipal Council in connection with the anti-Japanese movement, and they were settled justly in accordance with law.

Procurator’s Powers

“In his report, General Macnaghten said that certain property of the Chinese valued at $600,000 was forcibly stolen, that this property was subsequently sold and the offenders were dealt with arbitrarily and that a number of the so-called Chinese merchant traitors were illegally arrested and detained. The Court is unable to ascertain whether the above report is true or false. The powers of the Procurators of the Shanghai Special District Court are limited according to Articles 103/-186 of the criminal Code. Should the statement made by General Macnaghten regarding the above cases of forcible robbery of goods be correct, the Procurators of the Shanghai Special District Court cannot be held responsible for conducting the investigations into these cases.
General Macnaghten has blamed the Court for having ignored and failed to inquire into these cases but this is because he does not fully understand the competency of the Court. The statement made by General Macnaghten accusing the Court of having failed strictly to maintain the law in connection with the anti-Japanese boycott movement and his assertion that the attitude of the Court in this matter was one of the reasons for the recent Sino-Japanese Shanghai imbroglio, are perfectly erroneous. As General Macnaghten did not reveal the real reasons for his dissatisfaction when making his report, this Court is unable to offer any explanation or give a reply.”

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & S. D. REGISTRY No. D 3517 19. 4. 32.）

（批：Reference made to the main part letter as same subject in today's Chinese newspaper translation.）

《字林西报》，1932年4月18日，星期一

麦克纳顿将军
受批评

特区法院
阐明立场

指称缺乏
了解

上海特区法院秘书处在致各中文报纸的信中指出，前工部局总董E. B. 麦克纳顿准将在上周三举行的纳税人年会上就该机构发表某些言论时，表现出对上海特区法院确切地位缺乏了解，为此特致函如下：—

“针对4月14日各中文报纸刊登的关于前上海工部局总董麦克纳顿准将在外国纳税人年会上批评本院的报道，为避免公众误解，我们谨作如下解释：由于前工部局总董未能充分理解本院的管辖权限，故其所述内容与事实不符。

“必须指出，是否禁止民众爱国运动的问题属于行政当局的管辖范围。法院不可能越权行事。麦克纳顿将军声称法院与抗日运动持对立态度，这是由于他不了解法院的确切地位所致。自1931年9月18日以来，上海工部局已就抗日运动相关事项向法院提起三起诉讼，这些案件均依法得到公正审理。

检察官之权力

“麦克纳顿将军在报告中称，价值60万美元的华人财产被强行劫掠，随后该财产被变卖，罪犯受到任意处置，且多名所谓的‘华奸’商人被非法逮捕和拘留。法院无法核实上述报道的真伪。根据《刑法典》第103至186条之规定，上海特区法院检察官的权力是有限的。如果麦克纳顿将军关于上述货物强行抢劫案的陈述属实，上海特区法院的检察官无权负责对此类案件进行调查。

麦克纳顿将军指责法院忽视且未调查这些案件，但这正是因为他不完全了解法院的管辖权限。麦克纳顿将军指责法院在抵制日货运动中未能严格执法，并断言法院在此事上的态度是近期上海中日纠纷的原因之一，这些说法完全错误。由于麦克纳顿将军在报告时并未揭示其不满的真正原因，本院无法提供任何解释或答复。”

（印：上海公共租界警务处 中央及特别区登记处 编号 D 3517 19. 4. 32.）

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, APRIL 18, 1931.
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. S. S. D. REGISTRY.
No. 3517
Date 18 / 4 / 31

CHINESE & SHANGHAI
From General Macnaghten's strictures on the working of the Special District Courts, the Chinese members of the Council dissociated themselves. This was to be expected. It receives further illumination in the comment made on the retiring Chairman's speech by Chinese journals, as shown in yesterday's issue of the "North-China Daily News." The very circumstances which tended to hamper the Courts in their administration of justice have made it difficult at the present time for Chinese opinion to range itself openly with those who deplore the breakdown. The contention that the judges, in refusing to convict or to punish adequately persons charged with offences arising out of the boycott, were actuated by "patriotic" motives implicitly endorses the Council's complaints. It can however be looked upon in a sympathetic light, when it is realised how vehemently Chinese public opinion reacted to the Manchurian crisis in September last. When a Government is browbeaten to the point of resignation because of its alleged failure to deal properly with that crisis, it is unlikely that the judiciary can preserve the calm detachment demanded of it. So, however glaring may have been the Courts delinquencies, endorsement of their condemnation cannot be expected from Chinese at this moment, when the catastrophic effects of Japanese action are so fresh in the mind and so apparent to the eye. Yet General Macnaghten would have been failing in his duty if they had not expressed definite views on a matter of such vital importance. This was the more necessary because of the approaching end of the term of three years for which the Court Agreement stands.
Chinese criticism will be understood but it strays sadly from the point when it notes the absence from the retiring Chairman's speech of any specific reference to Japanese action. With the negotiations for the cessation of hostilities still in progress such reference might have been embarrassing and liable to misconstruction. Nor would it have been fair to the incoming Council to have attempted to sum up a case which it will eventually have to handle in the light of discussions elsewhere. General Macnaghten's appreciative tribute to the success of the Japanese and Chinese members in preserving their cooperative functions on
the Council throughout the crisis gained strength from reticence and wisely deferred the delivery of any verdict on episodes in which the Council was only one of several protagonists. Concerned as he was with the future of the Settlement, his acquittal of a failure to appreciate the Chinese point of view rests firmly on that tribute and on his plain enunciation of the need for taking that point of view into account when considering that future.
Chinese criticism, then, understandable up to a point, should not be looked upon as either negligible or final in its present form. It would be idle to expect a sudden reconciliation of Chinese and foreign views. When the mists surrounding Loyang are so dense, when the actual effects of recent events on Chinese policy are so hard to analyse, impetuous desires to test reconciliatory action have to be curbed. Once again, it may be urged, the blessed influence of a common effort in restoring normality must be allowed to have precedence, to develop its strength and, so, to pave the way for a calmer and more dispassionate discussion than is possible at the present time. On the Chinese side there will have to be, eventually, a clearer recognition of the fact that Shanghai's plight has been to foreigners as well as Chinese, a disaster of the first magnitude. Recovery from it imposes on every community an effort which should command the most unreserved spirit of cooperation. Foreigners will—many of them already have—come to appreciate the significance of the recent shattering of long-established convictions. Shanghai still remains however the essential pivot of China's economic and political progress. To safeguard that position must be the care of Chinese as much as foreigners. It is satisfactory therefore to observe that the same representatives who sat on the last Council have been re-elected by the Chinese organisations. Those representatives have shown their responsiveness to the opinions of their countrymen as well as their jealous regard for the integrity of Shanghai. They, no less than their colleagues, have a great opportunity for displaying their gifts of political foresight. They have the additional privilege of being able thereby, to make a substantial contribution to the solution of the intricate and infinitely more difficult problems of China as a whole.

《字林西报》，1931年4月18日，星期六。
上海公共租界警务处
中央及特别区登记处。
编号 3517
日期 18 / 4 / 31

中方与上海

鉴于麦克纳顿将军对特区法院工作的严厉批评，工部局华董与之划清界限。这是意料之中的事。正如昨日《字林西报》所示，中文报刊对离任总董演讲的评论进一步阐明了这一点。那些妨碍法院司法公正的情形，使得中国舆论目前难以公开与支持谴责法院失灵的人士站在一起。有人主张法官以“爱国”动机为由，拒绝定罪或充分惩罚因抵制运动而被指控犯罪的人，这种观点隐含地认可了工部局的投诉。然而，如果考虑到去年九月中国公众舆论对满洲危机反应之激烈，这种情况是可以令人同情的。当一个政府因其被指未能妥善处理该危机而遭受威逼直至辞职时，司法机关很难保持其所要求的冷静超然。因此，无论法院的失职行为多么显眼，在日本行动造成的灾难性后果仍历历在目、显而易见的当下，不能指望中国人会赞同对法院的谴责。然而，如果对如此至关重要的问题不表达明确观点，麦克纳顿将军便是失职。鉴于法院协议为期三年的任期即将届满，此举尤为必要。

中国人的批评是可以理解的，但当其指出离任总董的演讲中未具体提及日本行动时，便严重偏离了重点。鉴于停战谈判仍在进行中，此类提及可能会造成尴尬并易于被曲解。此外，试图总结一个最终需由继任工部局根据其他地方的讨论情况来处理的案件，对继任工部局也不公平。麦克纳顿将军赞赏地赞扬了日籍和华籍董事在整个危机期间在工部局保持合作职能方面的成功，这种克制增强了其言论的力量，并明智地推迟了对工部局仅为多方主角之一的插曲作出任何裁决。由于他关注的是租界的未来，他对于未能领会中方观点这一指责的辩白， firmly 建立在这一赞扬以及他明确阐述在考虑未来时必须顾及中方观点的基础之上。

因此，中国人的批评在一定程度上是可以理解的，但不应将其目前的形式视为无足轻重或最终定论。指望中外观点突然和解是不现实的。当洛阳周围的迷雾如此浓重，当最近事件对中国政策的实际影响如此难以分析时，必须抑制急于测试和解行动的冲动。可以再次强调，必须让共同努力恢复常态的神圣影响占据优先地位，使其力量得以发展，从而为比目前更冷静、更客观的讨论铺平道路。在中方方面，最终必须更清楚地认识到这样一个事实：上海的困境对外国人和华人而言都是一场巨大的灾难。从中恢复需要每个社区付出努力，这种努力应当赢得毫无保留的合作精神。外国人将——许多人已经——开始意识到近期长期确立的信念遭受粉碎的重大意义。然而，上海仍然是中国经济和政治进步的关键枢纽。维护这一地位必须是华人和外国人共同关心的事项。因此，令人满意的是，上一届工部局的相同代表已由华人组织重新当选。这些代表既表明了他们对本国同胞意见的反应灵敏，也表明了他们对上海完整性的深切维护。他们与其同事一样，拥有展示其政治远见才能的巨大机会。他们还享有额外的特权，即能够由此为中国整体复杂且极其困难的问题的解决做出实质性贡献。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, APRIL 15, 1932

SPECIAL DISTRICT
COURT

Chinese Answers Criticism
by Retiring Chairman

CAUSES OF LOCAL
TROUBLE

The "Shunpao," a leading Chinese newspaper, published yesterday a lengthy editorial comment regarding the criticisms of the Shanghai Special Area District Court made by Brig.-Gen. E. B. Macnaghten, the retiring chairman of the Shanghai Municipal Council, in his speech at the annual Foreign Ratepayers Meeting on Wednesday afternoon. A translation of the editorial follows:—

"After studying Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten's speech in detail, we feel and are convinced that his expressions are biased and that he has failed to recognise the fundamental nature of the local disaster. We feel that his opinions warrant some comment and now we are setting forth our arguments based on facts and reasons.

"Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten stated in his speech that the prejudiced actions of the Special Area District Court in anti-Japanese cases was one of the contributing factors in the cumulative causes which led to the actual warfare between the Chinese and Japanese military forces. If this statement had been given out by the Japanese, we would consider that they had been compelled to do it. But when it was Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten who made this statement, we cannot help but be puzzled.

"How did the anti-Japanese boycott movement start? Are there not any cumulative causes which forced us to launch this movement? If Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten does not consider the Japanese military activities as reasonable, he ought to realise the stimulus given to the feelings of the Chinese people as a result of the disaster in Manchuria last September as the cause of the anti-Japanese movement. The anti-Japanese movement, let it be known, has been carried out in a most peaceful manner through boycott of Japanese goods. No violence had been resorted to nor had the peace and order of the International Settlement been infringed upon. The security of the nationals of the friendly nations had never been endangered.

Boycott in America

"We declare that there was no ground for any interference with the patriotic movement thus carried out. Recently, an anti-Japanese boycott movement was started in the United States and we wonder what Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten would think about that.

"In connection with the local trouble, China has been making concession after concession, although realising that Japan was determined to precipitate the trouble. Despite her concessions, the desire to carry out wholesale murder on the part of the Japanese could not be checked and the manifestation of that desire caused a most tragic disaster.

"The present disaster to Japan is military encroachment while to China it is nothing other than self-defence. Peoples far away in Europe and America have expressed their sympathy with China. Yet Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten, an eye-witness of the trouble, has stood at the side of 'might is right.' Is it because of his biased thinking? Or is it because that Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten considers it right to conquer a country with military forces, to tear down international pacts and treaties, to break the peaceful state of the world and to overlook the international justice? That is what is puzzling us.

Provisional Court Agreement

"As to the Special District Court, this institution was reorganised from the Shanghai Provisional Court. The Provisional Court was an experiment provided by agreement signed by the Chinese Government and those interested Powers. Had this experiment failed to satisfy the interested nations, it would never have been reorganised into the present special district court. It also should be pointed out that the establishment of this court was also for the purpose of maintaining the sovereign integrity of the Chinese Government. Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten had no grounds to criticise the court for, if there is any evidence to show prejudiced action of the court in anti-Japanese cases, it is reasonable to assume that these actions were taken from patriotic motives.

"The establishment of the Special District Court was achieved by virtue of an agreement between the Chinese Government and the interested nations and we are of the opinion that Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten would not be permitted to act against an agreement so signed. Because of this belief, we feel that Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten has no chance of shaking the constitution of the Special District Court. This, we hope, the retiring chairman of the Council will note with care.

"Free City" Movement

"When we read Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten's speech carefully, we see that his goal is not a question pertaining to the Sino-Japanese hostilities, nor the Special District Court, but really the so-called 'Shanghai Question.' Recently, there have been cries for the establishment of a 'Greater Shanghai' or a 'Free City of Shanghai.' We wonder if Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten's stand for an international court is not the 'vanguard' of a 'free city' movement.

"If Brig.-Gen. Macnaghten's aim is really centering on this plan, we cannot but help considering his views as wrong. It must be made clear that not only this plan would be injuring the integrity of Chinese sovereignty, but it also must be realised that the Chinese people have awakened from their long nap and are now in their struggle for liberty and equality."

《字林西报》，1932年4月15日，星期五

特区
法院

离任主席批评遭中方驳斥

本地
事端之起因

中文大报《申报》昨日发表长篇社论，评论上海公共租界工部局董事会离任主席麦克纳顿准将（Brig.-Gen. E. B. Macnaghten）在周三下午举行的年度外侨纳税人大会上对上海特区地方法院所作的批评。该社论译文如下：——

“在详细研究麦克纳顿准将的演讲后，我们感到并确信，他的言论带有偏见，且未能认清本地灾祸的根本性质。我们认为他的观点值得加以评论，现基于事实与理由阐述我们的论点。

“麦克纳顿准将在演讲中称，特区地方法院在反日案件中的偏颇行为，是导致中日军队实际爆发战争的累积原因之一。如果此言出自日本人之口，我们会认为他们是迫不得已而为之。但既然此言出自麦克纳顿准将之口，我们不禁感到困惑。

“反日抵制运动是如何开始的？难道没有任何累积的原因迫使我们发起这场运动吗？如果麦克纳顿准将不认为日本的军事行动是合理的，他就应该意识到，去年九月满洲事变给中国人民感情带来的刺激，正是反日运动的原因。众所周知，反日运动是通过抵制日货的方式，以最和平的方式进行的。未曾诉诸暴力，也未侵犯国际租界的和平与秩序。友邦国民的安全从未受到威胁。

美国的抵制运动

“我们声明，对于如此开展的爱国运动，没有任何干涉的理由。最近，美国也发起了反日抵制运动，我们不知麦克纳顿准将对此作何感想。

“关于本地事端，中国虽明知日本决意挑起事端，但仍一再让步。尽管中国作了让步，日本方面进行大规模屠杀的欲望仍无法遏制，而这种欲望的显现导致了极为惨痛的灾难。

“目前的灾难对日本而言是军事侵略，对中国而言则是自卫。远在欧洲和美洲的人民已表达对中国的同情。然而，作为事端目击者的麦克纳顿准将，却站在‘强权即公理’的一边。这是因为他的思想有偏见吗？还是因为麦克纳顿准将认为，以武力征服一个国家、撕毁国际公约和条约、破坏世界和平状态以及无视国际正义是正确的？这正是令我们困惑之处。

临时法院协定

“至于特区地方法院，该机构是由上海临时法院改组而成。临时法院是中国政府与有关列强签署协定所设立的一项实验。如果这项实验未能令有关国家满意，它绝不会改组为现在的特区地方法院。还应指出，设立此法院也是为了维护中国政府的主权完整。麦克纳顿准将无权批评该法院，因为如果有证据显示法院在反日案件中有偏颇行为，合理推测这些行为是出于爱国动机。

“特区地方法院的建立是基于中国政府与有关国家之间的协定，我们认为，麦克纳顿准将不应被允许违背如此签署的协定。基于这一信念，我们觉得麦克纳顿准将没有机会动摇特区地方法院的体制。我们希望工部局离任主席能仔细注意这一点。

‘自由市’运动

“当我们仔细阅读麦克纳顿准将的演讲时，我们发现他的目标并非涉及中日敌对行动或特区地方法院的问题，而实际上是所谓的‘上海问题’。最近，有人呼吁建立‘大上海’或‘上海自由市’。我们怀疑，麦克纳顿准将主张设立国际法院，是否就是‘自由市’运动的‘先锋’。

“如果麦克纳顿准将的目标确实集中在此计划上，我们不得不认为他的观点是错误的。必须明确的是，该计划不仅会损害中国主权的完整，而且必须认识到，中国人民已从长眠中觉醒，现在正为自由和平等而奋斗。”

General Rapped By Chinese
Press For Criticism Of Court

Retiring S.M.C. Chairman's Speech At Meeting
Of Ratepayers Yesterday Target Of Attack
In Bitter Editorial Today

Holding that the criticism of the Special District Court, made by Brigadier General E. B. Macnaghten, retiring chairman of the Shanghai Municipal Council, in his speech before Settlement ratepayers at the Carlton Theater yesterday afternoon were groundless, the Shun Pao, one of the leading vernacular dailies of the city, this morning made a target of the general's remarks, in a lengthy editorial under the title of "Attention to Brigadier General Macnaghten's Speech at the Foreign Ratepayers' Meeting." A liberal translation f the editorial follows:

"Brigadier-General E. B. Macnaghten, in his capacity as the retiring chairman of the Shanghai Municipal Council, made a lengthy report to the annual meeting of the foreign ratepayers yesterday in which he stated that the prejudiced rulings of the Special District Court in anti-Japanese cases was 'one of the contributing factors in the cumulative causes which led to actual warfare between the Chinese and Japanese military forces.' In conclusion, Brigadier-General Macnaghten also made a definite suggestion for the establishment of an international court.

Bias Charged

"After studying Brigadier-General Macnaghten's speech in detail, we feel and are convinced that his expressions are biased and that he has failed to recognize the fundamental nature of the local disaster. We feel that his opinions warrant some comment and now we are setting forth our argumentation based on facts and reasons.

"Brigadier-General Macnaghten stated that the prejudiced actions of the Special District Court in anti-Japanese cases was one of the contributing factors in the cumulative causes which led to actual warfare between the Chinese and Japanese military forces. If this statement had been given out by Japanese, we would consider that he had been compelled to do it. But when it was Brigadier-General Macnaghten who made this statement, we cannot help but be puzzled.

Boycott Recalled

"How did the anti-Japanese boycott movement start? Are there not any cumulative causes which precipitated us to launch this movement? If Brigadier-General Macnaghten does not consider the Japanese activities as reasonable, he ought to realize the stimulus given to the feelings of the Chinese people as result of the disaster last September in Manchuria as the cause of the anti-Japanese movement. The anti-Japanese move-

ment, let it be known, has been carried out in a most peaceful manner through boycott of Japanese goods. No violence had been resorted to and nor had the peace and order of the International Settlement been infringed upon. The security of the nationals of the friendly nations had never been endangered.

"We declare that there was no ground for any interference with the patriotic movement thus carried out. Recently an anti-Japanese boycott movement was started in the United States and we wonder what Brigadier-General Macnaghten would think about this action.

"Wholesale Murder"

"In connection with the local trouble, China has been making concession after concession, although realizing that the Japanese had determined to precipitate and provoke the trouble. Despite her concessions, the desire to carry out wholesale murder on the part of the Japanese could not be checked, and the manifestation of that desire caused a most tragic disaster.

"This present disaster to Japan is military encroachment while to China it is nothing other than self-defense. Peoples far away in Europe and America have expressed sympathy towards our country. Yet Brigadier-General Macnaghten, an eye-witness of the trouble, has stood at the side of 'might is right.' Is it because of his biased thinking? Or is it because that Brigadier-General considers it right to conquer a country with military force, to tear down international pacts and treaties, to break the peaceful state of the world and to overlook international justice? That is what is puzzling us.

"Might Is Right"

"We, however, concur with Brigadier-General Macnaghten in his opinion that the present trouble exposed the weakness of the International Settlement. But these weaknesses, from our view, constitute the failure of the authorities to check the outbreak of the trouble

因批评法院遭中文报刊抨击

工部局离任主席在昨日纳税人大会上的演讲
成为今日严厉社论的攻击目标

《申报》作为本市主要中文日报之一，认为上海公共租界工部局董事会离任主席麦克纳顿准将（Brigadier General E. B. Macnaghten）昨日下午在卡尔登戏院向租界纳税人发表的演讲中对特区地方法院的批评毫无根据，今晨在一篇题为《注意麦克纳顿准将在外侨纳税人大会上的演讲》的长篇社论中，将这位将军的言论作为攻击目标。该社论的自由翻译如下：

“上海公共租界工部局董事会离任主席麦克纳顿准将（E. B. Macnaghten）在昨日的年度外侨纳税人大会上作了长篇报告，他在报告中称，特区地方法院在反日案件中的偏颇裁决是‘导致中日军队实际爆发战争的累积原因之一’。最后，麦克纳顿准还明确建议设立一个国际法院。

被指存有偏见

“在详细研究麦克纳顿准将的演讲后，我们感到并确信，他的言论带有偏见，且未能认清本地灾祸的根本性质。我们认为他的观点值得加以评论，现基于事实与理由阐述我们的论点。

“麦克纳顿准将称，特区地方法院在反日案件中的偏颇行为，是导致中日军队实际爆发战争的累积原因之一。如果此言出自日本人之口，我们会认为他是迫不得已而为之。但既然此言出自麦克纳顿准将之口，我们不禁感到困惑。

回顾抵制运动

“反日抵制运动是如何开始的？难道没有任何累积的原因促使我们发起这场运动吗？如果麦克纳顿准将不认为日本的行动是合理的，他就应该意识到，去年九月满洲事变给中国人民感情带来的刺激，正是反日运动的原因。反日运

动，众所周知，是通过抵制日货的方式，以最和平的方式进行的。未曾诉诸暴力，也未侵犯国际租界的和平与秩序。友邦国民的安全从未受到威胁。

“我们声明，对于如此开展的爱国运动，没有任何干涉的理由。最近，美国也发起了反日抵制运动，我们不知麦克纳顿准将对此行动作何感想。

‘大规模屠杀’

“关于本地事端，中国虽明知日本决意挑起并激化事端，但仍一再让步。尽管中国作了让步，日本方面进行大规模屠杀的欲望仍无法遏制，而这种欲望的显现导致了极为惨痛的灾难。

“目前的灾难对日本而言是军事侵略，对中国而言则是自卫。远在欧洲和美洲的人民已表达对我国的同情。然而，作为事端目击者的麦克纳顿准将，却站在‘强权即公理’的一边。这是因为他的思想有偏见吗？还是因为这位准将认为，以武力征服一个国家、撕毁国际公约和条约、破坏世界和平状态以及无视国际正义是正确的？这正是令我们困惑之处。

‘强权即公理’

“然而，我们同意麦克纳顿准将的观点，即目前的事端暴露了国际租界的弱点。但从我们的观点来看，这些弱点构成了当局未能遏制事端爆发的失败

"When we read Brigadier Gen-

we see that his goal is not a ques-
tion pertaining to Sino-Japanese
hostilities, nor the Special District
Court, but really the so-called
'Shanghai Question.' Recently

be tolerated. If Brigadier General
Macnaghten is viewing the Chinese

pelled to feel that progress in his
mind has been very slow, record-
ing nothing of an improvement in
a period of 30 years."
Few Japanese Out
The absence of Japanese ratepay-
ers was conspicuous at the Rate-

lack of public interest was shown
by the absence of visitors in the
public gallery. This is in contrast
to meetings of other years when
the gallery was crowded, parti-

the purchase of the Majestic Hotel

At the annual meeting yesterday
the report and accounts for the
past year and the Budget for 1932
were passed without discussion. The
election of two Chinese members
of the Land Commission
was proposed in the form of a re-
solution by the Chairman. Opposi-
tion was made by Mr. E. F. Harris
to the proposal who submitted an
amendment which Mr. A. W. Bur-
kill, the chairman, was at first in-
clined to reject on technical
grounds.
Three Distinct Interests
Winning his point, Mr. Harris
addressed the meeting. He stated
that his main objection to the
resolution was the admission of two
instead of one Chinese member to
the Commission. He maintained
that the Land Commission is es-
sentially a tribunal or arbitration
board representing three distinct
interests, the landowners, the
Council and the ratepayers.
Mr. Harris contended that in a
composition of three these interests
were equally and properly repre-
sented. If two more members were
added, a proper and equal repre-
sentation of the necessary interests
involved would be impossible, he
said, suggesting the appointment of
only one Chinese Commissioner.
Wider Cooperation
Supporting the Council's resolu-
tion, Mr. Norman Lewis said that
it had been the avowed principle
of the Shanghai Municipal Coun-
cil to extend wider facilities to the
Chinese for cooperation with the
Council. The admission of two
Chinese members of the community
to the Land Commission was held
as a step in the right direction.
The amendment lost by a small
majority when it was voted upon.
Withdrawal of the candidature of
Mr. J. W. T. Brooke from the con-
test for ratepayers' representative
on the Land Commission left the
field to Messrs. H. S. Peek and H. G.
Robinson as candidates.
Addressing the meeting before a
vote was called, Mr. Peek explain-
ed his reasons for seeking the post.
He said that thereby a ratepayer
would be elected who had definite
interests in land in the city and
had, on one occasion, acted as the
property owners' representative on
the Commission. Mr. Robinson did
not address the meeting. On a
show of hands Mr. Peek was elect-
ed.

“特区法院的设立是依据中国政府与有关各国之间的协议而实现的，我们认为，麦克纳格顿准将不被允许采取违背此类签署协议的行动。基于这一信念，我们认为麦克纳格顿准将没有机会动摇特区法院的体制。我们希望将军能仔细注意这一点。”

对“自由市”的看法

“当我们仔细阅读麦克纳格顿准将的演讲时，我们发现他的目标并非涉及中日敌对行动的问题，也不是特区法院问题，而实际上是所谓的‘上海问题’。最近一直有呼声要求建立‘大上海’或‘上海自由市’。我们怀疑麦克纳格顿准将主张设立国际法庭，是否正是‘自由市’运动的‘先锋’。

“如果麦克纳格顿准将的目标确实集中在这个计划上，我们不得不认为他的观点是错误的。必须明确的是，这种‘国中之国’的计划不仅会损害中国主权的完整，而且必须认识到，中华民族已从长期的沉睡中充分觉醒，意识到为自由和平等而战的必要性。这样的计划绝不会被容忍。如果麦克纳格顿准将像30年前那样看待中国人，我们不得不感到他的思想进步非常缓慢，在30年间没有任何改进的记录。”

日本人出席者寥寥

在昨天的纳税人会议上，日本纳税人的缺席引人注目，旁听席上访客稀少也显示出公众缺乏兴趣。这与往年的会议形成对比，往年旁听席总是拥挤不堪，特别是在讨论购买 Majestic Hotel（大华饭店）地块作为市政中心，或允许新闻代表列席工部局会议等事项时。

在昨天的年度会议上，过去一年的报告和账目以及1932年预算案未经讨论即获通过。主席以决议形式提议选举两名华人担任土地委员会成员。E. F. Harris 先生对该提案提出反对，并提交了一项修正案，主席 A. W. Burkill 先生起初倾向于以技术理由驳回该修正案。

三种截然不同的利益

Harris 先生得逞后向会议发言。他表示，他反对该决议的主要理由是接纳两名而非一名华人委员进入委员会。他坚持认为，土地委员会本质上是一个代表三种截然不同利益的法庭或仲裁机构，即地主、工部局和纳税人。

Harris 先生辩称，由三人组成的结构能够平等且适当地代表这些利益。他说，如果再增加两名成员，就不可能对所涉及的各项必要利益进行适当且平等的代表，因此建议仅任命一名华人委员。

更广泛的合作

Norman Lewis 先生支持工部局的决议，他说，上海公共租界工部局一贯公开的原则是为华人提供更广泛的设施以与工部局合作。接纳两名社区华人成员进入土地委员会被视为朝着正确方向迈出的一步。

该修正案在表决中以微弱多数被否决。J. W. T. Brooke 先生退出土地委员会纳税人代表的竞选，使得候选人只剩下 H. S. Peek 先生和 H. G. Robinson 先生。

在表决前向会议发言时，Peek 先生解释了他寻求该职位的理由。他说，由此将选出一位在城市土地拥有确切利益、并曾一度在委员会中担任业主代表的纳税人。Robinson 先生未向会议发言。经举手表决，Peek 先生当选。
